data.expected_signal: Off-grid outputs for 0<|x|<2^-6: q != q.to(float8_e4m3fn).to(float32), and no flush-to-zero below 2^-10.
data.metric: grid membership q == q.to(float8_e4m3fn).to(float32) plus equality vs x.to(float8_e4m3fn).to(float32)

evidence.summary: Subnormal region defect confirmed. Explicit sweep of 101 magnitudes in [2^-13, 2^-6]: 75/101 kernel outputs are not e4m3-representable (q != q.to(float8_e4m3fn).to(float32)) and all 75 differ from the true e4m3 cast reference. Flush-to-zero is absent: all 5 tiny inputs (1e-5 ... 4e-4) whose e4m3 reference is exactly 0.0 come back nonzero (e.g. x=1e-5 -> 9.5367e-06, ref 0.0). Critically, this fires on a plain benign input: torch.randn(4096) has 65 elements with 0<|x|<2^-6, and 45 of them produce off-grid outputs / mismatch the e4m3 reference (max abs err 9.765625e-04 = half the 2^-9 subnormal step); 0 mismatches in the normal region, so the failure is exactly localized to the subnormal band as claimed.

rationale: Lines 15-17 derive step purely from floor(log2|x|) with no lower clamp on the exponent, so the grid keeps refining below the format's smallest normal instead of holding at the 2^-9 subnormal spacing; outputs therefore fall between e4m3 codes.

scope_evidence.summary: "The contract is that every value is rounded to the nearest representable e4m3 value" and "e4m3 has 4 exponent bits and 3 mantissa bits" - the named format fixes the representable set, including its subnormals, and no input range restriction is given.
Artifact contains only kernel.py, meta.json (status=under_test, passed=null) and problem.txt; there is no test.py narrowing the input domain, so the prose contract governs.

scope_rationale: problem.txt states the contract as "every value is rounded to the nearest representable e4m3 value" and names the format by its exponent/mantissa widths; the subnormal region is part of the e4m3 value set, not an exotic extension. No test.py exists, so the prose contract is the operative criterion and the input distribution is unrestricted; I use ordinary randn plus a small-magnitude sweep, both admitted by "a float32 tensor".
statement: For 0 < |x| < 2^-6 = 0.015625 (the e4m3 subnormal region), the kernel keeps using a relative step 2^(floor(log2|x|)-3) instead of the fixed subnormal step 2^-9, so it returns values that are not representable in e4m3 (e.g. x=0.001 stays ~0.001 instead of snapping to a multiple of 2^-9=0.001953125, and |x|<2^-10 is not flushed to 0). Metric: elementwise q != q.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).to(torch.float32) grid-membership, plus comparison against x.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).to(torch.float32). Representative in-scope input: torch.randn(4096) on CUDA, where ~1% of elements land below 2^-6, plus an explicit sweep of magnitudes in [2^-12, 2^-6].

data.expected_signal: For |x|>448 kernel emits 512/1024/... which are not e4m3-representable; differs from saturating clamp(x,-448,448) reference.
data.metric: grid membership + equality vs clamp-then-cast and vs torch direct cast

evidence.summary: Overflow/no-saturation defect confirmed. On 20 inputs +/-[416,448,449,460,464,500,512,1000,4096,1e4], 11 kernel outputs exceed the e4m3 max finite 448 and are not representable (snap(kernel) collapses each to 448): x=464->480, 500->512, 1000->1024, 4096->4096, 1e4->10240, and negatives. Both candidate references agree and disagree with the kernel on exactly those 11 elements: torch's direct cast x.to(float8_e4m3fn) and the saturating clamp(x,-448,448)-then-cast both give 448/-448 (torch saturates rather than NaN here). Values <=448 (416, 448) are handled correctly, and 449/460 happen to round down to 448 correctly, so the failure begins at 464.

rationale: Lines 15-17 impose no upper clamp on the exponent, so the code extrapolates the 8-per-binade grid indefinitely past the format's largest binade.

scope_evidence.summary: "round a float32 tensor to the nearest value representable in the FP8 e4m3 format" - representability is the stated requirement, and e4m3 has no finite values above 448; input magnitudes are not restricted.

scope_rationale: The contract names e4m3 and requires the output to be a representable e4m3 value; the format's finite range (max 448) is part of that named value set. With no test.py, problem.txt's unrestricted "a float32 tensor" admits large-magnitude inputs, which are exactly the regime FP8 storage kernels must saturate.
statement: For |x| above the e4m3 max finite value 448, the kernel applies no saturation or overflow handling, so it emits magnitudes such as 512, 1024, 4096 that do not exist in e4m3 (e.g. x=1000 -> step 64 -> 1024). Under either overflow convention (OCP saturating cast to 448, or torch.float8_e4m3fn's NaN) the output is wrong. Metric: grid membership q == q.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).to(torch.float32) and comparison to the saturating reference clamp(x, -448, 448)-then-cast, over inputs like [448.0, 449.0, 500.0, 1000.0, 1e4] and their negatives.

data.expected_signal: At/near exact powers of two in [2^-6,256], check whether floor(tl.log2) picks the wrong binade -> off-grid output or >6.25% relative error.
data.metric: grid membership + exact equality vs x.to(float8_e4m3fn).to(float32) over powers of two, nextafter neighbors, and 400k log-uniform normal-range samples

evidence.summary: Binade-selection risk not realized on this backend. 90 boundary inputs (exact powers of two 2^-6..2^8 within range, plus float32 nextafter neighbors on both sides, and negatives): 0 off-grid outputs, 0 mismatches vs x.to(float8_e4m3fn).to(float32), max relative deviation from input 1.19e-07 (i.e. exact hits). A dense log-uniform sweep of 400,000 samples covering the pure normal range [2^-6, 448) and its negatives also gave 0 off-grid outputs and 0 mismatches vs the e4m3 cast reference, with max relative error 0.0588 < the 0.0625 contract bound and 0 samples exceeding it. So tl.log2+floor selects the correct exponent everywhere tested, and the normal-range path (including tie behavior encountered by this distribution) matches the e4m3 reference exactly; the confirmed defects are confined to the subnormal band (c1) and above-448 overflow (c2).

rationale: tl.log2 is typically a fast approximate device intrinsic on fp32; floor() of an approximate log2 is discontinuous exactly at binade boundaries, so any 1-ULP error flips the selected step by a factor of two. This must be decided by runtime probe, not source reading.

scope_evidence.summary: "within any binade it can represent 8 evenly spaced values ... the resulting relative error is bounded by half a mantissa step, about 2^-4 = 6.25%" - a wrong binade breaks both the grid and the stated error bound.

scope_rationale: problem.txt requires every value to round to the nearest representable e4m3 value and explicitly bounds the relative error by half a mantissa step (~6.25%); powers of two and their neighbors are ordinary float32 inputs inside the format's normal range, so a mis-selected binade there violates a stated requirement. No test.py exists to narrow the domain.
statement: Binade selection via e = floor(tl.log2(|x|)) is a floating-point computation; at or just below exact powers of two (e.g. 2^-6, 1.0, 8.0, 256.0, and nextafter-below values like 7.9999995) a sub-ULP error in tl.log2 can pick the neighboring exponent, yielding a step 2x too fine (off-grid output, e.g. 8.5 inside the [8,16) binade) or 2x too coarse (error up to 12.5%, exceeding the contract's stated half-mantissa-step bound). Metric: for a sweep of exact powers of two 2^-9..2^8 and their nextafter neighbors, check grid membership q == q.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).to(torch.float32) and max relative deviation from x.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).to(torch.float32).
